title: UppASD benchmark campaign manifest (v1)
description: Declarative description of one benchmark campaign (TERMINOLOGY.md CAMPAIGN, docs/UppASD Production Benchmark Framework.md section 15, WP-09): which cases/variants/sizes, which backends and precisions, at how many samples, under which environment-quality policy. A campaign manifest names cells to execute and leaves execution itself to the harness (WP-03/06) -- it is a declaration, not a script. Machine hardware policy (concrete OpenMP thread counts) is deliberately NOT baked in here: 'cpu.thread_policy' names a policy that benchmarks/harness/campaigns.py resolves against whatever host actually runs the campaign (benchmarks/harness/omp_topology.py), the same live-queried-never-hardcoded principle omp_topology.py already uses throughout.

id_list_or_all.description: Either the literal 'ALL' (every id the referenced case manifest declares) or an explicit, non-empty list of ids.

id.description: Campaign identifier. This is what appears as campaign_id in every record the campaign produces.

tier.description: LEAN (harness development, developer sanity, gross regression detection -- never authoritative for crossover claims) or FULL (production characterization: all core workload families, practical size ladders, broad OpenMP scaling, sufficient independent samples, strict provenance and environment-quality gating). TERMINOLOGY.md CAMPAIGN.

backend_scope.description: CPU_ONLY, CUDA_ONLY, or CPU_AND_CUDA. A LEAN campaign normally covers both backends at reduced scope (blueprint section 15). Among FULL campaigns, full_cpu.yaml is CPU_ONLY, full_cuda.yaml is CUDA_ONLY, and full_crossover.yaml is CPU_AND_CUDA -- the only manifest whose CPU-BEST and CUDA cells are guaranteed to share one campaign_id/build/source-revision by construction (blueprint section 10: never pair CPU-BEST from a different campaign run against this campaign's CUDA cells).

cases.description: Which case/variant/size cells this campaign covers. Every case_id must resolve against benchmarks/cases/ at load time (benchmarks/harness/campaigns.py); an authoritative (tier FULL) campaign may never resolve to an infrastructure_test_only case (benchmarks/harness/cases.py::require_not_infrastructure_only).

cpu.description: Required when backend_scope is CPU_ONLY or CPU_AND_CUDA; absent otherwise. thread_policy names a machine-hardware-policy resolution rule (benchmarks/harness/campaigns.py), never a concrete thread-count list: LEAN_SAMPLE resolves to {1, a moderate count, the host's full physical-core count} (blueprint section 15 'OMP 1 + one moderate + one large thread count'); FULL_PHYSICAL_SWEEP resolves to every thread count from 1 to the host's physical-core count (blueprint section 15 'broad OpenMP scaling' / TERMINOLOGY.md CPU-1T..CPU-BEST). Both always exclude SMT siblings (blueprint section 9: 'prioritize physical cores in the standard campaign').

gpu.description: Required when backend_scope is CUDA_ONLY or CPU_AND_CUDA; absent otherwise. Only CUDA is represented among the four standard campaign tiers -- HIP performance claims require real HIP hardware and are out of scope here (blueprint section 4). GPU memory admission (blueprint section 14/WP-06 section E, 'all five workload families where GPU memory permits') is a runtime decision made per (case, size, precision) against the actual queried device (benchmarks/harness/gpu_memory.py, benchmarks/harness/gpu_campaign.py::build_unavailable_memory_record) -- it is not, and cannot be, predicted in this manifest.

single_campaign_execution.description: Required true when backend_scope is CPU_AND_CUDA. Documents and machine-checks blueprint section 10's crossover requirement: this manifest's CPU and CUDA cells are executed together, under one campaign_id and one build/source revision -- never assembled after the fact from an arbitrary separately-run CPU campaign merely because a GPU campaign happened to start separately.

sample_count.description: Target repeated-sample count per cell (TERMINOLOGY.md SAMPLE). LEAN campaigns use a small count (harness development, gross regression detection only); FULL campaigns require at least 5, matching blueprint section 15 'sufficient independent samples' / section 13 'at least five valid timing samples where reasonable'.

measurement_profile.description: DYNAMICS_ONLY (the primary computational benchmark, blueprint section 7) or PRODUCTION_LIGHT (fixed representative measurement cadence). Do not mix the two in one crossover claim (blueprint section 7).

environment_quality_mode.description: DEVELOPER (blueprint section 14: 'developer runs should remain usable even when some quality flags are present', runner.run_sample's default require_clean_environment=False) or STRICT (blueprint section 14: 'authoritative campaigns should support a strict environment mode that refuses unsuitable samples', runner.run_sample's require_clean_environment=True). LEAN campaigns must use DEVELOPER; FULL campaigns must use STRICT.

report_banner.description: Required, and fixed to this exact text, when tier is LEAN: every generated report for a LEAN campaign must prominently state this (blueprint section 15, TERMINOLOGY.md CAMPAIGN). Forbidden when tier is FULL -- a FULL/authoritative report carries no such disclaimer.
report_banner.const: LEAN CAMPAIGN — NOT AUTHORITATIVE FOR CROSSOVER CLAIMS

allOf.$comment: LEAN tier: small repeat count is allowed, DEVELOPER environment mode, and the report banner is mandatory.
FULL tier: at least 5 samples, STRICT environment mode, and no report banner (that disclaimer is LEAN-only).
CPU_ONLY: a cpu block is required; no gpu block and no single_campaign_execution flag.
CUDA_ONLY: a gpu block is required; no cpu block and no single_campaign_execution flag.
CPU_AND_CUDA: both blocks are required, and the single-campaign-execution guarantee must be explicitly affirmed.
